name: 31941-loraswap-gptoss20b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (sm90), one a3 node, --gres=gpu:1.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, EP off. One engine on one GPU, so every adapter buffer is whole on the one device.
architecture: GptOssForCausalLM sparse MoE, 24 layers, hidden 2880, 32 experts with 4 active per token, mxfp4 expert weights (~13 GB); the rest is readable off the checkpoint's config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=1 (floor 1, ceiling 4), 100 requests, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, 1800 s safety cap, static seed 31941. One request in flight is load-bearing: the declared quantity is per-request, and added streams let requests sharing a tag queue behind one another.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no chat template, no shared prefix, temperature 0, ignore_eos: ~1600 prompt tokens (1520-1680) and ~200 output tokens (190-210) per request. Every request carries one of the eight adapter tags in `scenario.json` (`spec.backend.lora_modules`), drawn uniformly at random; all eight names point at one set of weights, so what they buy is eight distinct tags.
purpose: A long-prompt document assistant serving eight customer-specific adapters, one request at a time on a single GPU.
launch:
# Every key here goes into AsyncEngineArgs: an unknown key is a TypeError at engine construction.
# `--lora-modules` is API-server surface and is NOT an EngineArgs field -- the eight adapter names
# are declared client-side, in `configs/scenario.json` `spec.backend.lora_modules`.
# `max-loras: 1` against eight host-cached adapters is part of the declaration, not a tuning knob.

model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
tensor-parallel-size: 1
enable-lora: true
max-loras: 1
max-cpu-loras: 8
max-lora-rank: 32
max-num-seqs: 8
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.95
enable-prefix-caching: false
trust-remote-code: true
max-model-len: 4096
